findings.title: AssignmentSource default timestamp is fixed at import time
findings.body: queued: datetime = timezone.now() in a dataclass evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued receives the same stale timestamp. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now). This makes the recorded time incorrect and can mislead any future logic or metrics based on it.

findings.title: Cycle guard suppresses all outbound syncs for an integration, not just the triggering issue
findings.body: should_sync returns False whenever the source integration id matches the target installation's integration id, but AssignmentSource does not identify the triggering external issue. If a group is linked to multiple external issues from the same integration, an inbound assignment from one issue suppresses outbound sync to all of them, leaving the other linked issues with stale assignees. Consider carrying and checking the external issue id/key, or explicitly accepting this limitation.

findings.title: AssignmentSource is serialized with a raw datetime and deserialized without coercion
findings.body: to_dict uses asdict, so the Celery kwargs built in sync_group_assignee_outbound contain queued as a datetime object. That is not a plain JSON-safe value; if the task serializer stringifies it, from_dict will later construct an AssignmentSource whose queued is a string rather than a datetime. Serialize queued to an ISO string, or omit it, and parse it back in from_dict.

findings.title: Source-integration outbound tasks are still enqueued and discarded later
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues sync_assignee_outbound for every linked external issue even when assignment_source identifies the source integration. Tasks for source-integration issues will only exit after fetching ExternalIssue, Organization, integration, and installation and checking should_sync. In rapid webhook scenarios this still creates avoidable Celery load; filtering out source-integration external issues before enqueuing would be more efficient.

findings.title: Missing coverage for deassign suppression and cross-integration sync
findings.body: The added tests only cover assignment suppression for a matching integration. There is no test that deassignment with a matching AssignmentSource is also suppressed, nor that assignments sourced from one integration are still propagated to a different integration. Those are the main behaviors changed by this PR, so regressions could go unnoticed.
